coaching.headline: We kicked the door in and took the base. Keep that finish; clean up the duo deaths.
coaching.team: This was a convincing win with actual follow-through. Early Fangtooths and Mini Prime were followed by a huge structure advantage and an inhibitor finish. The blemish was the duo dying together again before the enemy took Fangtooth. That sequence deserves attention, but it does not turn a dominant team performance into a fucking disaster.

focus.title: Make the reset call together
focus.action: When either Murdock or Phase dies before a major objective, call a fresh plan immediately: regroup for a viable contest, or choose a safe trade. Check whether the surviving duo partner makes it through that reset.

perPlayer.78c58fb9-a3cb-44bd-99e5-9a08a16ece1c: DrabeyBaby did the fucking job: the strongest hero damage in the lobby and most of our objective damage. Keep that combination. When a gank opens the map, name the next objective and get a follow-up call before starting it. Khaimera should lead the decision as well as the damage, especially if the duo has just gone down.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs made Legion and Argus miserable, and the damage backed it up. The part to tighten is surviving alongside Phase: both died in the same sequence more than once. When Phase falls or cannot support the next trade, Murdock breaks off toward the team and rebuilds a safe firing line. Keep the aggression; make the reset just as decisive.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: A dead healer has a pretty shit benefits package. Mr_Meat31 supplied the most healing in the match, but Phase also died repeatedly, including alongside Murdock. Against Grux or Aurora closing in, keep a safe pull destination and call the retreat before the carry is immobilized. Preserve the healing contribution by making the exit a shared call, not two separate guesses.
perPlayer.55ce8bb7-8577-43b5-a6ea-a62219fa5447: Destri stayed alive and farmed hard, but Belica's hero damage lagged behind his usual output. Keep the survival; the next step is turning that economy into a complete follow-up. When the frontline catches a reachable target, chain Seismic Assault into Void Bomb from safety, then judge the ult by the target's missing mana instead of dumping everything automatically.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy kept Zarus alive and farmed steadily. Keep that discipline and make the next commitment count. On the next grouped push, name the Coliseum target and confirm Murdock or Belica can follow before committing. Make the arena a team invitation, not a private fucking appointment.

18.6.call: Murdock and Phase died in this sequence before the enemy Fangtooth. Reassess the contest after those deaths; the remaining players need one agreed plan.

20.7.call: Our tower gains overlapped their lone Outer Tower. Keep the useful trade; check the exposed lane before committing everyone to the next push.

22.4.call: The final kills were followed by two inhibitors. That is the finish to repeat: take the base opening instead of extending the hunt.

matchup: Aurora and Argus both held Tainted Scepter, suppressing Khaimera's healing.
Surviving the first control effects matters more than a damage-only comparison.
build: Sky Splitter, Ashbringer, Onixian Quiver and Imperator form a coherent attack and critical-damage plan.
Ashbringer's cooldown reduction is once per ability, not on every hit.
eternal: Thraex, Savage Strikes and Ferocity all reward sticking to one target, which is his kit.
The healing runs into two Tainted Scepters; Golden Mane is the slot-two alternative at the cost of Ferocity's attack speed.
augment: Feral Ambush adds 10% range to the leap that opens his combo: engage reach, not damage.
Jungle Invasion only beats it when invading is the plan; there is no basis to call either better here.
crest: Eviscerator fits as a follow-up once Khaimera is committed, not as an opener from range.
Its omnivamp loses value whenever Aurora's or Argus's Tainted Scepter is on him.
improvement: If Aurora or Argus cuts entries short, compare Absolution over Imperator, trading critical damage for magical armor and tenacity.
This strong game does not establish that the swap was needed.

matchup: The enemy duo died five times before minute ten to our one; first blood was Murdock's on Argus.
Of Murdock's three deaths, Argus got two and Grux one.
build: Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Imperator support catching and finishing targets.
None of it protects Murdock from Argus or Grux reaching him.
eternal: Vermis and Serration reward repeated attacks and finishing damaged targets.
Melting Point needs armored targets, and no final inventory had an armor item, though that is not conclusive.
For a future draft like this, Sub-Surface trades that offense for protection against area abilities from Iggy & Scorch and Aurora.
augment: Justice's Reach lets Shots Fired pierce a minion wave from a safer distance.
Martial Law suits a snowballing game like this one; neither is proven better by this record.
crest: Pacifier supports the aggressive build with a dash, finishing damage and a possible recast.
Chasing with the dash spends a tool that could separate him from Grux or Aurora; keep it when mobility serves the plan.
improvement: Keep the damage core unless surviving magical pressure becomes the limit.
Dread over Imperator adds magical armor and a magical-damage block, sacrificing critical damage.
Sub-Surface is a future minor alternative to Melting Point, not an in-match swap.

matchup: Legion's Malady punishes targets under 40% health, so heals matter most before Murdock drops that low.
Aurora's and Argus's Tainted Scepter cut healing on whoever Phase is healing.
build: Grux's self-healing gave Tainted Scepter's anti-heal a relevant target.
The bigger question is whether Prophecy's personal damage deserves priority over helping a strong Murdock survive control.
eternal: Fragrance's close-range requirement can conflict with a safe position against Grux and Aurora.
Exarch is a future draft alternative, trading Lotus's random growth for empowering a linked Murdock.
augment: Psychic Support only pays when the Linked carry is short on mana, which this record cannot show.
Kindred Surge suits a duo escaping dives; Final Flash trades Energy Lance length for damage.
crest: Tranquility fits the job, helping the duo through incoming damage when alive and in range.
There is no reason to replace it based on the ward count alone.
improvement: First comparison: Enra's Blessing over Prophecy, shielding an immobilized Murdock at the cost of Phase's basic-attack damage.
If magical pressure is killing Phase, Devotion adds magical armor and stronger low-health ally heals, at that offense's cost.
Keep Tainted Scepter when Grux's sustain is the problem.

matchup: Iggy & Scorch was the enemy's top hero damage, with zones that punish prolonged exposure.
Punish extended spell use without walking into Iggy's setup just to force the trade.
build: Orb of Enlightenment, Noxia and Megacosm reward a completed spell sequence.
The build has real damage tools, so lower recorded output alone does not justify blaming the items.
eternal: Early Bloom complements the leveling plan with Combat Veteran and Orb of Enlightenment.
Keep safe casting positions against Iggy's zones rather than chasing Fragrance's bonus.
Immaculate is a future slot-two alternative, trading close-range damage for full-health protection.
augment: Combat Veteran supports progression and repositioning; calling it no combat value is misleading.
A damage augment is an alternative to test, not a repair justified solely by this match's lower damage.
crest: Epoch's stasis answers Grux and Aurora committing onto Belica, if the team covers the exit.
A deathless match neither proves it saved her nor proves it was wasted.
improvement: Keep Noxia and the leveling package; a single lower-output win does not isolate an item problem.
If fights demand immediate burst, compare Combustion with the Orb slot, giving up level-scaled health and cast healing.
Do not infer purchase timing from the final evolved Orb.

matchup: Aurora chains slow, root and stun, and her Tainted Scepter anti-heal lands on Zarus's lifesteal plan.
Aurora scored the only kill on Zarus in the match.
build: Augmentation, Mutilator and Basilisk reward weaving basics; Basilisk's shred also helps Khaimera and Murdock.
It has value without enemy armor purchases, though actual shred uptime is not established.
eternal: Marrow, Leech and Roses ask Zarus to be in the middle of fights and finishing them.
Two enemy Tainted Scepters cut Marrow heals; Jealousy is the slot-two alternative at the cost of Roses' gold.
augment: Master Of Spears pays when Zarus throws Spear Of Nyr for bonus damage on low-health targets.
Flow State is the dive-and-reset alternative; neither is proven better here.
crest: Soulbearer is not literally wasted, given magical-power scaling on Spear of Nyr and Evade.
Brutallax is more direct into Aurora's control, adding a cleanse but trading away Soulbearer's shield and movement burst.
improvement: Test Brutallax in a future draft against Aurora rather than blaming Soulbearer in a one-death game.
Keep the item core and its shared armor shred.
If magical pressure stops the engage, compare Legacy with a damage slot, trading offense for magical armor.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s), Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Our damage is 4/5 physical — predictable; the enemy itemizes one armor item against most of it. A magical pick would split their defenses.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Ambush leap → Unleash AS → Cull stun, Invigorate to cleanse+heal
ourKits.winCondition: stick on one target, stun with Cull and out-sustain via Spirit Regen
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his Cull stun
ourKits.playAgainst: ANTI-HEAL is mandatory — it guts his whole kit; kite the leap and CC through Invigorate

ourKits.combo: Telekinetic Link an ally → Psychic Flare blind → Energy Lance → Hyperflux buff ult
ourKits.winCondition: buff a hyper-carry through the Link and Hyperflux for a teamfight
ourKits.passive: abilities heal her and her linked ally
ourKits.playWith: the strongest carry to Link and supercharge
ourKits.playAgainst: kill the linked carry, not Phase; break the link timing

ourKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
ourKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

ourKits.combo: Evade in → Barricade block → Spear of Nyr (execute <20%) → Coliseum ult arena
ourKits.winCondition: trap a target in Coliseum and out-duel with stacked Gladiator
ourKits.playWith: a team that joins him inside the Coliseum
ourKits.playAgainst: don't fight him in his arena — disengage; burst through Barricade's window

ourKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
ourKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
ourKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
ourKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
ourKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

enemyKits.combo: Smash 'n Grab pull → Crush knockup → Warlord's Challenge stun → bleed-stacked basics
enemyKits.winCondition: land the pull→knockup chain to lock a target while bleed and AS shred them
enemyKits.passive: basics stack a bleed for sustained damage
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his knockup/stun window
enemyKits.playAgainst: telegraphed engage — bait Crush/Pull, then punish; kite his slow start

enemyKits.combo: Oil Spill → Molotov ignite → Flame Turret → Inferno knockback ult
enemyKits.winCondition: layer fire zones on a choke/objective and burn the team
enemyKits.playWith: CC that holds enemies in his fire
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't fight in his zones — flank; kill the turret, dive him

enemyKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
enemyKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

enemyKits.combo: Dread Nova stun → Ether Crystal push/lift → Particle Shredder channel → Synaptic Obliterator beams
enemyKits.winCondition: poke from max range and zone with the crystal
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline to protect his stationary channel
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Dread Nova; dive him during the immobile ult channel

loadout.name: Feral Ambush

ability.name: Ambush
ability.what: Leap to an Enemy Hero or Monster, dealing 75/105/135/165/195 (+80%) physical damage and Slowing them by 40% for 1.35s.

loadout.plain: Ambush reaches a bit farther, so you can start fights or finish a fleeing low target from a safer distance. Since Ambush hits harder on wounded enemies, the extra reach mostly wins chases.

loadout.name: Thraex
loadout.text: Mark the last Enemy Hero damaged by your Basic Attack for 3s, increasing your damage against them by 3% (+0.4% per level) and reducing the damage they deal to you by 1.5% (+0.35% per level).
loadout.plain: Your basic attacks mark whoever you are hitting, so once Unleash starts its flurry you deal more to that target and take less back from them. Best in long one-on-one brawls against a single diver.

loadout.name: Savage Strikes
loadout.text: Deal 1.5 (+0.4 per level) Physical Damage On-Hit. Attacking an Enemy Hero increases this by 100% for 3s, stacking up to 3 times. Heal for the damage dealt.
loadout.plain: Small extra damage and healing on every hit that grows while you keep attacking a hero. Unleash's fast flurry stacks it quickly, giving steady sustain in extended fights.

loadout.name: Ferocity
loadout.text: Gain 1% Total Attack Speed per 1s in Hero Combat, stacking infinitely.
loadout.plain: Your attack speed keeps climbing the longer you stay in a hero fight, which feeds more Rage and faster cooldowns. Pays off in drawn-out brawls, does little in quick burst trades.

loadout.name: Eviscerator
loadout.text: Rending Strikes:  Gain 20% Attack Speed and 8% Omnivamp for 6s. Empower your Basic Attacks to deal (+10%) Damage On-Hit for 6s.
loadout.plain: Extra attack speed, lifesteal on everything and empowered basic attacks for a short window. Use it with Unleash for a burst of fast, healing hits on one target.

loadout.name: Feral Ambush

ability.name: Ambush
ability.what: Leap to an Enemy Hero or Monster, dealing 75/105/135/165/195 (+80%) physical damage and Slowing them by 40% for 1.35s.

loadout.plain: Ambush reaches a bit farther, so you can start fights or finish a fleeing low target from a safer distance. Since Ambush hits harder on wounded enemies, the extra reach mostly wins chases.

loadout.name: Thraex
loadout.text: Mark the last Enemy Hero damaged by your Basic Attack for 3s, increasing your damage against them by 3% (+0.4% per level) and reducing the damage they deal to you by 1.5% (+0.35% per level).
loadout.plain: Your basic attacks mark whoever you are hitting, so once Unleash starts its flurry you deal more to that target and take less back from them. Best in long one-on-one brawls against a single diver.

loadout.name: Savage Strikes
loadout.text: Deal 1.5 (+0.4 per level) Physical Damage On-Hit. Attacking an Enemy Hero increases this by 100% for 3s, stacking up to 3 times. Heal for the damage dealt.
loadout.plain: Small extra damage and healing on every hit that grows while you keep attacking a hero. Unleash's fast flurry stacks it quickly, giving steady sustain in extended fights.

loadout.name: Ferocity
loadout.text: Gain 1% Total Attack Speed per 1s in Hero Combat, stacking infinitely.
loadout.plain: Your attack speed keeps climbing the longer you stay in a hero fight, which feeds more Rage and faster cooldowns. Pays off in drawn-out brawls, does little in quick burst trades.

loadout.name: Eviscerator
loadout.text: Rending Strikes:  Gain 20% Attack Speed and 8% Omnivamp for 6s. Empower your Basic Attacks to deal (+10%) Damage On-Hit for 6s.
loadout.plain: Extra attack speed, lifesteal on everything and empowered basic attacks for a short window. Use it with Unleash for a burst of fast, healing hits on one target.
